correctness.rationale: The established planar convex Cheeger inner-parallel theorem reduces the full functional minimization to a uniquely soluble area identity. Erosion distributes over intersection; the circular-quadrant area is integrated exactly, yielding the active scalar equation and the closed threshold. Strict nesting proves monotonicity. Direct cap and tangent-corner expansions give independently checkable coefficients 8/(3*pi) and 1/sqrt(pi), with bounded remainders. The included high-precision checker validates sample roots and expansions, without being used as a proof of the continuum claim.

value.rationale: Corner clipping is a natural geometric interpolation between the disk and square, and the exact point at which changes stop affecting the Cheeger minimizer is a nontrivial parameter-dependent rigidity phenomenon. The active interval has a unique exact implicit law, and two distinct sharp boundary exponents (3/2 and 2) reveal geometric mechanisms of tangent caps and corners. This is a complete phase description with natural consequences for Cheeger shape sensitivity, not an arbitrary evaluation at isolated parameters.
